issues.description: PR does three things instead of one — split it
issues.detail: The stated goal is 'add POST tests for things_advanced.' But this diff also rewrites the README example (style reformatting, handle() signature change, status formatting change, str.format conversion, bounded_stream swap) and adds an FAQ entry. Three patches masquerading as one. Reviewing this is a chore because the test change is buried under reformatting noise. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: README handle() signature reordered to (req, resp, ex, params) — wrong order, will break
issues.detail: Falcon's error handler signature is (req, resp, ex, params) in modern versions but the original README had (ex, req, resp, params). If you're 'fixing' the README to match current API, fine — but this is an undocumented drive-by change in a PR titled 'add POST request tests.' The commit message says nothing about it. Maintainer six years from now will curse the author. Either justify it in the commit message or drop it.

issues.description: FAQ example handler has bad taste — nested if/else where a flat structure works
issues.detail: The PostTest.on_post in the FAQ has if/else inside if/else when it could be three flat branches or a single expression. This is example code in user-facing docs; readers copy it. Special-cases the empty-body case twice (None-or-0 check, then 'or 0' fallback inside read). BAD-TASTE. Write the example you'd want a beginner to imitate.

issues.description: Switching req.stream to req.bounded_stream in the example is a semantic change unmentioned in the description
issues.detail: The PR description says 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' but the actual diff swaps to req.bounded_stream.read() with no argument. These behave differently under WSGI when Content-Length is wrong or absent. The description and the diff disagree. Pick one, justify it, document why. Right now the commit message lies about what landed.

issues.description: FAQ test uses assert(result.status == ...) — parenthesized assert is a Python footgun
issues.detail: `assert(x, y)` is a tuple and always truthy. `assert(x)` works but reads like a function call and trains readers toward the broken form. In example code that teaches testing, write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400`. Small thing, but you're publishing it as canonical.

issues.description: New test cases reuse a magic Authorization token with no shared fixture
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 both hardcode `'Authorization': 'custom-token'` and `'Content-Type': 'application/json'`. Existing tests above presumably do the same. Pull the common headers into a local dict at the top of the test. Not a blocker, but the diff would have been smaller and the next addition cheaper.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The actual test additions are fine and useful — POST happy-path plus the empty-body-with-Content-Length edge case is exactly the kind of thing that should be tested. But this PR is three patches in a trench coat: tests, an unrelated full reformat of the README example (including a handle() signature change that nobody mentioned), and a new FAQ section whose example code has questionable taste. Split it. Land the test PR cleanly. Resubmit the README reformat as its own diff with a commit message that says what changed and why. Fix the FAQ example to be code you'd want imitated.
